questions.stem: A client with a tibia fracture in a cast reports pain rated 9 out of 10 that isn't relieved by the prescribed opioid. Pain increases when the nurse gently moves the toes. What does the nurse suspect?

rationale.correct: Compartment syndrome: severe pain unrelieved by opioids and pain with passive stretch come early; pulselessness is late.

perOption.a: Pain out of proportion to the injury and pain on passive stretch are the earliest signs.
perOption.b: Expected pain is relieved by analgesics.
perOption.c: Fat embolism causes respiratory and neurologic signs.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.stem: The nurse suspects compartment syndrome in a client with a casted forearm. What should the nurse do first?

options.text: Notify the provider immediately and keep the arm at heart level
Elevate the arm above the heart
Apply ice and reassess in 2 hours

rationale.correct: Compartment syndrome: notify right away, keep the limb at heart level, loosen dressings and prepare for fasciotomy.

perOption.a: Prompt notification allows bivalving the cast or a fasciotomy; elevating above the heart reduces blood flow.
perOption.b: Raising it above the heart can reduce arterial flow further.
perOption.c: Delay can lead to permanent damage.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.stem: Two days after a femur fracture, a client suddenly becomes confused and short of breath and has petechiae across the chest. What does the nurse suspect?

rationale.correct: Fat embolism usually appears 24 to 72 hours after a long bone fracture.

perOption.a: Fat droplets from long bone fractures cause respiratory distress, confusion and petechiae.
perOption.b: Pneumonia develops more gradually and doesn't cause petechiae.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: Which assessments are part of a neurovascular check of an injured extremity? Select all that apply.

options.text: Movement of the fingers or toes

rationale.correct: Check the 6 P's: pain, pallor, pulse, paresthesia, paralysis and poikilothermia (temperature).

perOption.a: Increasing pain can signal ischemia.
perOption.b: Pallor or cyanosis suggests poor perfusion.
perOption.c: Weak or absent pulses suggest arterial compromise.
perOption.d: Numbness or tingling suggests nerve compression.
perOption.e: Weakness suggests nerve or muscle damage.
perOption.f: These aren't part of a neurovascular check.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.stem: A client has a new cast on the lower leg. Which statement shows a need for more teaching?

options.text: "I'll keep my leg raised for the first day or two."
"I'll use a coat hanger to scratch under the cast."

rationale.correct: Cast care: elevate, keep it dry, don't put objects inside and report neurovascular changes.

perOption.a: Elevation reduces swelling.
perOption.b: Objects can break the skin and cause infection.
perOption.d: Moisture weakens the cast and damages the skin.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: An older adult fell at home. Which finding suggests a hip fracture?

options.text: The affected leg is shorter and rotated outward
The affected leg is longer and rotated inward
Full range of motion without pain

rationale.correct: Hip fracture: shortening, external rotation and groin or hip pain.

perOption.a: These are classic signs of a hip fracture.
perOption.b: This isn't typical.
perOption.c: This doesn't indicate a hip fracture.

questions.stem: A client had a posterior-approach total hip replacement. Which statement shows a need for more teaching?

options.text: "I'll keep a pillow between my legs."
"I'll cross my legs when I sit."
"I won't bend forward to pick things up."

rationale.correct: Posterior hip precautions: no flexion beyond 90 degrees, no crossing the legs and no inward rotation.

perOption.a: This avoids bending the hip more than 90 degrees.
perOption.b: This keeps the hip abducted.
perOption.c: Crossing the legs can dislocate the hip.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

rationale.correct: Report suspected dislocation immediately and keep the leg still.

perOption.a: Sudden pain with shortening and rotation suggests dislocation.
perOption.b: This isn't expected.

questions.stem: Which intervention best reduces the risk of deep vein thrombosis after total knee replacement?

options.text: Early walking with prescribed anticoagulants and compression devices
Keeping a pillow under the knee

rationale.correct: After joint replacement: anticoagulation, mechanical compression, early mobility and hydration.

perOption.a: Mobility and prophylaxis reduce venous stasis.
perOption.b: This can cause flexion contracture.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: The nurse is checking a client's crutch use. Which observation requires correction?

options.text: The client rests body weight on the axillary pads
There are 2 to 3 finger widths between the armpit and the crutch pad
The elbows are flexed about 30 degrees
The crutch tips are 15 cm (6 inches) to the side of the feet

rationale.correct: Crutches: weight on the hands, a 2 to 3 finger gap at the armpit and elbows flexed 20 to 30 degrees.

perOption.a: Pressure on the armpits can damage the brachial plexus; weight goes on the hands.
perOption.b: This is the correct fit.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.stem: A client with a right leg injury is using crutches. How should the client go up stairs?

options.text: Step up with the left (uninjured) leg, then bring up the crutches and the right leg
Step up with the right leg first

rationale.correct: Stairs: up with the good leg, down with the crutches and the injured leg.

perOption.a: "Up with the good, down with the bad."
perOption.b: The injured leg can't bear the lift.
perOption.c: The good leg leads going up.

questions.stem: A client has weakness in the left leg. How should the client use a cane?

options.text: Hold the cane in the right hand and move it forward with the left leg
Hold the cane in the left hand
Move the cane with the right leg
Hold the cane far in front of the body

rationale.correct: Cane: on the strong side, advanced with the weak leg.

perOption.a: The cane on the strong side supports the weak leg.
perOption.b: The cane goes on the strong side.
perOption.c: The cane moves with the weak leg.
perOption.d: It should be about 15 cm (6 inches) to the side.

Step forward with the strong (left) leg
Lift the walker and move it forward about one step's length

perOption.a: The walker moves first to provide a base of support.

questions.stem: Which instruction helps prevent osteoporosis?

options.text: Get enough calcium and vitamin D and do weight-bearing exercise
Smoke fewer than five cigarettes a day

rationale.correct: Osteoporosis prevention: calcium, vitamin D, weight-bearing exercise, no smoking, limited alcohol and fall prevention.

perOption.a: These build and maintain bone mass.
perOption.b: Cola may reduce bone density.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: A client is prescribed alendronate. Which statement shows correct understanding?

options.text: "I'll take it first thing in the morning with a full glass of water and stay upright for 30 minutes."
"I'll take it with breakfast and coffee."
"I'll take it with my calcium pill."

rationale.correct: Bisphosphonates: empty stomach, plain water, upright for 30 minutes, no other food or medications for 30 minutes.

perOption.a: This prevents esophageal irritation and allows absorption.
perOption.b: Food and drinks other than water reduce absorption.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate whether it is more typical of osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis.

rows.text: Morning stiffness lasting more than 1 hour
Bony nodes at the finger joints closest to the nails (Heberden's nodes)
The same joints affected on both sides of the body
Joint pain that worsens with use and improves with rest
Fatigue, low-grade fever and weight loss

rationale.correct: OA: degenerative, worse with use, Heberden's nodes. RA: autoimmune, symmetric, long morning stiffness, systemic symptoms.

perOption.r1:c1: OA stiffness usually lasts under 30 minutes.
perOption.r1:c2: Prolonged morning stiffness is typical of RA.
perOption.r2:c1: Heberden's nodes are typical of OA.
perOption.r2:c2: RA affects the knuckles and wrists rather than causing these nodes.
perOption.r4:c1: Wear-and-tear pain is typical of OA.
perOption.r4:c2: RA pain is often worse after rest.
perOption.r5:c2: RA is a systemic autoimmune disease.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.stem: A client with gout is learning about diet. Which food choice shows a need for more teaching?

rationale.correct: Gout: limit purines (organ meats, shellfish), alcohol and fructose; drink fluids.

perOption.a: Low-fat dairy may lower uric acid.
perOption.b: These are high in purines and raise uric acid.

questions.stem: A client with gout is prescribed allopurinol. Which statement shows a need for more teaching?

options.text: "I'll take it every day to prevent attacks."
"I'll take it to stop the pain of an attack."

rationale.correct: Allopurinol prevents gout by lowering uric acid; it doesn't treat acute flares.

perOption.a: Allopurinol is a long-term preventive drug.
perOption.b: Allopurinol doesn't treat acute attacks; colchicine, NSAIDs or steroids do.
perOption.d: A rash can signal a serious reaction.

questions.stem: A client had an above-the-knee amputation 2 days ago. Which position helps prevent a hip flexion contracture?

options.text: Lying prone several times a day
Keeping a pillow under the residual limb
Sitting in a chair most of the day
Keeping the head of the bed raised all day

rationale.correct: After amputation: prone positioning, no pillows under the limb after 24 hours and limited sitting.

perOption.a: Lying face down stretches the hip flexors.
perOption.b: This promotes hip flexion contracture (after the first 24 hours).

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

options.text: "Phantom limb pain is real, and we can treat it."

rationale.correct: Phantom limb pain is real; it may be treated with medications, mirror therapy and other approaches.

perOption.a: Phantom pain comes from nerve signals and responds to treatment.
perOption.b: This dismisses a real experience.

questions.stem: How should the nurse wrap a below-the-knee residual limb with an elastic bandage?

options.text: In a figure-eight pattern, with firmer pressure at the end of the limb
In circular turns, tightest near the knee

rationale.correct: Residual limb wrapping: figure-eight, distal to proximal, firmest at the end.

perOption.a: This shapes the limb into a cone for a prosthesis.
perOption.b: This restricts blood flow.
perOption.d: Wrapping is usually continuous, rewrapped several times a day.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: When a client holds both wrists in full flexion for 60 seconds, numbness and tingling occur in the thumb, index and middle fingers. Which condition does this suggest?

rationale.correct: Carpal tunnel: positive Phalen and Tinel signs; wrist splinting and ergonomic changes help.

perOption.a: A positive Phalen test suggests median nerve compression.
perOption.b: Gout causes joint inflammation.
perOption.c: This isn't the Phalen test result.
perOption.d: This involves color changes with cold.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
